Subject: Re: Sudden drop in throughput / 504s during Black Friday run — urgent

Quick update from runtime diagnostics. Weve reproduced locally against the Polaris sample traffic. Root cause appears to be a rare header truncation bug in the client SDKs streaming parser where very large multipart headers (X-Polaris-Meta) are split across frames and the SDK dechunker drops trailing bytes when the header boundary aligns with a mid-frame packet under backpressure. The server-side runtime sees malformed header blocks and drops the connection, resulting in timeouts and reduced throughput.

Reproducer steps (short):
- Run the attached reproducer-instructions.md against SDK v2.4.3 with small write windows and high concurrency.
- Observe header lengths > 4K and intermittent connection resets.

Immediate mitigations were preparing:
- Canary patch for the SDK dechunker that preserves fragmented header frames (will ship as v2.4.4-canary).
- Runtime fallback: temporarily accept truncated headers and re-request missing metadata via a second request where safe.

Attaching: sdk-headers-pcap.txt (trimmed) for your SREs. Were estimating a canary out in ~2 hours; will update with a PR and release notes.

- Marcus
Engineering, Redwood Inference
